"Interstate's original network consisted of an 860-mile line that supplied the Midwest with gas from the southwest Kansas and Texas panhandle."

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded LengthKnown=860 mi matches exactly, on two independent sources, the length of the ORIGINAL 1929 mainline built by Interstate Pipe Company (renamed Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line in 1932) from the southwest Kansas/Texas Panhandle producing area into the Midwest -- the specific line this GEM entry is scoped to. Wikipedia's Panhandle Eastern article and the Encyclopedia.com Panhandle Eastern Corporation entry independently state '860 miles'/'860-mile line'; both documents were already opened on this row for other columns (Wikipedia: Fuel/Location/Owner/Start/Status; Encyclopedia.com: Start) and are read here to exhaustion for Length too. Note for context, not a discrepancy: the modern PEPL system (this original line plus later expansions/laterals) is reported at ~6,000-6,300 mi in the 2021 SEC 10-K and Wikipedia -- that is the present-day full network, not the recorded 860 mi figure, so no conflict with the sheet value.

verifications.note: "It is owned by Energy Transfer, and operated by Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Company, LP."

2021 Form 10-K filed by registrant Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Company, LP: "The Company owns and operates a large natural gas open-access interstate pipeline network," consisting of the Panhandle, Trunkline and Sea Robin transmission systems (the Panhandle system's ~1,300-mile mainline runs from the Anadarko Basin of Texas/Oklahoma/Kansas through Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio into Michigan -- this pipeline). Same filing also names Southern Union Panhandle LLC as the 1% general partner and Energy Transfer as 99% limited partner of PEPL, consistent with the sheet's already-staged Owner1 'Southern Union Panhandle LLC' / AggregateOwners 'Southern Union Panhandle LLC; Energy Transfer'.
